key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite; petiole bases dilated/winged and often fused across the node into a disc; blades ovate, sometimes 3-lobed.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Usually solitary, sometimes 2–3; rays light orange-yellow, often brown/purple-lined beneath.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypselae often with pappus absent or minute.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: At an intact opposite-leaf node, look for widened/winged petiole bases connecting across the stem into a nodal disc; this is the strongest practical recognition feature.; Perennial/subshrub with coarse hairy stems and ovate, sometimes three-lobed, opposite leaves.; Heads commonly single or in twos or threes; rays light orange-yellow, often dark-lined on undersides.; Compare Simsia lagasceiformis: usually annual, with different nodal-disc and root habit; do not rely on pappus absence alone, as it overlaps.; Crew photo sequence: whole plant; front/side node macro; underside of head; mature fruit with scale.
